title: Wernicke Encephalopathy: Classic Triad and Frequent Omissions
subject: Medical Triads
preview: Wernicke encephalopathy is associated with thiamine deficiency and may cause confusion, eye movement abnormalities and ataxia.
quickRevision: Wernicke encephalopathy is associated with thiamine deficiency and may cause confusion, eye movement abnormalities and ataxia.
Early parenteral thiamine is important when suspected, particularly in high-risk nutritionally depleted patients.
Untreated disease can cause lasting memory impairment and evolve into Korsakoff syndrome.

sections.title: Recognize the pattern
points: Wernicke encephalopathy is associated with thiamine deficiency and may cause confusion, eye movement abnormalities and ataxia.
The classic triad is frequently incomplete; risk includes malnutrition and alcohol use disorder but is not limited to them.

sections.title: What this finding does—and does not—mean
points: Early parenteral thiamine is important when suspected, particularly in high-risk nutritionally depleted patients.
Untreated disease can cause lasting memory impairment and evolve into Korsakoff syndrome.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: The absence of ophthalmoplegia or ataxia must not falsely reassure when risk and confusion are present.
